correctness.rationale: The degree-block lex-min upper-triangle code is exactly complete for tournament isomorphism, since all and only degree-preserving permutations are tried. Every n-vertex tournament arises from an (n-1)-vertex one by an incidence mask, so the recursive canonical extension is exhaustive. Joint directed refinement uses old colour and both in/out neighbour counts, and stabilizes by monotone partition refinement. Replayed counts 1,1,2,4,12,56,456 iso and 1,1,2,4,12,55,451 C2; exact nonsingleton code sets validated, with explicit nonisomorphic six-vertex cyclic-triple witnesses. Scope n<=7 only.

originality.rationale: The asserted contribution is the complete n<=7 two-variable counting-equivalence partition of all uncoloured tournaments, not general existence of ambiguous tournaments. The most relevant stronger theorem, Kiefer (2020), Thm 6.29 and 6.26, already characterizes individual identification for edge-coloured partially oriented graphs and implies regular/paired-cycle mechanisms. However, it does not state the exact 55/451 type numbers or complete four-way n=7 nontrivial class partition; McKay catalogs isomorphism types but not C2 equivalence. Multiple semantic searches of existing published mathematical findings found no equivalent indexed claim. Unindexed older exact tables remain a real originality risk.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed exact C2/1-WL tournament-type tabulation could subsume the finite 55/451 counts.

Kiefer 2020 theorem is substantially stronger at individual identifiability, so mere existence of ambiguous six-vertex or regular seven-vertex witnesses is not original and is deliberately not presented as the new contribution.
Computational exhaustiveness depends on the packaged canonical-extension and refinement implementation, but both completeness arguments are made explicit.

value.rationale: Directed complete relations are a standard natural class for finite-variable counting logic. Determining the exact first ambiguity layer and the entire next layer is a motivated natural finite classification: n=6 has precisely one doubleton while n=7 has three doubletons and one regular tripleton, rather than all score-equivalent tournaments simply coalescing. These are explicit, reusable correctness benchmarks and exact finite-model expressivity invariants; the result is not just a renamed regularity observation.
